## Assay role

ELISA converts antibody-dependent color intensity into an estimated serum sIgA concentration. It is a separate assay lane from sequencing.

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
  S[Serum dilution] --> W[Three technical replicate wells]
  STD[Standards + blanks + controls] --> OD[Plate optical density]
  W --> OD
  OD --> C[Calibration + dilution correction]
  C --> Q[Replicate and range QC]
  Q --> V[One participant sIgA estimate]
```

| Raw data | Processed data | Final integration value |
|---|---|---|
| plate, well, replicate, OD, dilution | blank-corrected OD, back-calculated concentration, CV, flags | one reviewed concentration per participant |

The presentation’s seven-point 1.250-to-0 µg/ml curve and reported $R^2=0.959$ describe assay development, not automatic plate acceptance. The laboratory must lock the kit, lot, sample dilution, incubation/read settings, calibration model, LLOQ/ULOQ, control limits, CV threshold, and repeat rules.

## QC gate

Inspect standards and residuals, blank behavior, control recovery, saturation, dilutional parallelism, replicate precision, edge/plate effects, and censor flags. Do not silently turn values below LLOQ into zero or average a failed well into the result.

::: {.callout-important title="What the assay does not generate"}
It does not count mucosal plasma cells, sequence IgA, measure stool IgA coating, or directly report intestinal secretion. It produces an accessible serum concentration with assay uncertainty.
:::
